company_name: Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited
model: Lender FCFE at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment expense in FY2023-FY2025 cash-flow add-backs or equity notes (last charge RMB1.1m in FY2023; share option scheme general mandate of 155.6m shares unused as at the H1 FY2026 interim). SBC-zero market convention: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1756 derived from Yahoo USDHKD=X 7.8456 / USDCNY=X 6.6739 at 2026-10-22T04:02Z; direct CNYHKD=X quote 1.175 agrees. No A-share or secondary listing exists for a parity check; the FY2025 dividend of HKD0.36 was declared in HKD on RMB earnings, so the dividend yield at the quote is unaffected by the bridge.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,014,204,924 issued ordinary shares at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim note 15), unchanged since the US$90m convertible bond fully converted in FY2025 (+122.7m shares). No options granted under the scheme, no treasury shares, no dilutive instruments outstanding; the weighted average basic and diluted counts for H1 FY2026 are both 2,014.2m. Held flat: perpetual bonds (RMB1.66bn 'other equity instruments') are serviced through the tax-and-minorities line, not as dilution.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is the COST OF EQUITY, in CNY, because the discounted flow is free cash flow to equity. Build: China 10-year CGB ~1.8% + equity risk premium 7.0% for China H-shares x beta 1.1 (wholesale-funded non-bank lender with ~1.9x gearing and no deposit franchise, plus a hospital operator under DRG/DIP reimbursement reform) = ~9.5%, plus 2.0pts for central-SOE governance (capital allocation can follow SASAC directives), HK small-cap illiquidity and refinancing dependence on bank lines and CULC bonds = 11.5% base. Bear 13.5% (credit-cycle and policy stress), bull 10.5%. Bracketed by house comparables: 0998.HK 10.5%, 2016.HK 11.0% (deposit-funded joint-stock banks), 1788.HK 11.5% (HK broker). Discounting CNY flows at a CNY rate; the HKD bridge is applied to the per-share result only.
inputs.lease_treatment: The group is predominantly a LESSOR. 'Principal portion of lease payments' in financing activities (FY2025 RMB676m, FY2024 178m, FY2023 717m) is sale-and-leaseback and lease-liability funding of the leasing book, i.e. part of the RMB49.5bn wholesale funding stack; its interest (RMB29.5m on lease liabilities in FY2025) sits inside finance-segment cost of sales and finance costs, which are above PBT. Hospital property leases are immaterial (lease liabilities RMB48m at FY2024). Treated once, inside the profit flow; no separate lease charge in the driver paths.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests (RMB108.6m of FY2025 profit; RMB4.16bn of equity, mainly minority holders in hospital subsidiaries) and perpetual-bond holders ('other equity instruments', RMB52.2m of FY2025 profit, RMB1.66bn of equity) are deducted INSIDE the flow via the cash_tax_rate_path, which is defined as (income tax + NCI share + perpetual coupons) / PBT = 28.5% on FY2025 actuals (701.6 + 108.6 + 52.2) / 3,019.1. The engine's post-'tax' EBIT is therefore profit attributable to ordinary owners of the parent. Nothing is deducted again in an equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: lender-style FCFE capitalised at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net_debt held at zero (house convention for banks and lenders: 0998.HK, 2016.HK, 1788.HK). WHY NOT OWNER-FCF: the financial-parser flagged that statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 +RMB5.8bn, H1 FY2026 +0.3bn, FY2023 +5.0bn, FY2024 +1.1bn) contains new finance leases written and lease receipts, while RMB1.6-2.3bn/yr of interest paid sits in financing activities; the RMB49.5bn of borrowings fund the RMB71bn interest-earning lease/factoring book and are operating funding, not net debt to subtract from an EV. The hospital business is consolidated inside the same flow and funded from the same balance sheet, so the parts are not valued separately. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = group revenue (finance interest income + healthcare sales); ebitda_margin_path = (profit before tax + D&A) / revenue, i.e. the margin is AFTER all funding costs and credit impairments; da_pct_path = D&A / revenue; cash_tax_rate_path = (tax + NCI + perpetual coupons) / PBT so post-tax EBIT equals profit attributable to ordinary shareholders; capex_pct_path = da_pct_path + equity capital that must be retained to support asset growth (attributable equity / total assets = 23.0% at 30 June 2026, applied to the asset growth each scenario implies, plus hospital growth capex above D&A); wc_capture_pct = 0, sbc = 0, no leases. FCF therefore equals FCFE = attributable net income minus required retention, and 'wacc' is the cost of equity. FY0 (FY2025) last_fcf = 1,575 is normalised FCFE: attributable profit 2,156.8 less a normalised 3%-asset-growth retention of ~582 (statutory FY2025 assets actually fell 2%, which would make FCFE look higher than sustainable). LATEST EVIDENCE: H1 FY2026 revenue -6.3% YoY (finance -12.5% as asset yields repriced lower, healthcare -6.9% under DRG/DIP) but profit attributable +2.8% to RMB1,262.5m because funding costs fell faster than yields (NIM 4.42% vs 4.34%) and healthcare costs were cut; finance segment PBT 1,457m (+3.8%), healthcare segment PBT 288.5m (-14.6%). Finance is ~84% of PBT despite healthcare being ~65% of revenue. No numeric FY2026 guidance; 30% payout maintained for 11 years, FY2025 dividend HKD0.36 (~8.0% yield at the quote). Price is an intraday HKEX print, not after-hours. At the quote the stock trades at ~0.38x attributable book (HKD11.65/share), ~3.5x trailing EPS (RMB1.08 = HKD1.27) and ~8% yield; the model's answer that it is worth well above the quote is the arithmetic of a ~12% ROE lender at an 11.5% cost of equity trading at 0.38x book, and the weights are skewed to bear (35%) because the discount reflects durable SOE-governance and policy risks rather than a mispricing that is certain to close. The bear case (CoE 13.5%, ROE compressing to ~7-8% as DRG/DIP losses deepen, NIM normalises and credit costs rise) lands close to the current price, i.e. the market is pricing roughly the bear case as its central case.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run revenue growth settles at 3% (base path), well below every historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Attributable equity CAGR (12.4% 5-yr) exceeds EPS CAGR (2.4% 5-yr) by far more than 30%. Equity growth is inflated by issuance (shares +17% since FY2020: 2021 placement, FY2025 convertible conversion plus two strategic placements) and by retaining 70% of earnings while ROE fell from 16.3% (FY2020) to 11.8% (FY2025). Equity CAGR is NOT a usable growth proxy here; revenue CAGR (11.9%) is acquisition-driven healthcare consolidation that has now reversed (H1 FY2026 -6.3%).
historical_growth.notes: fcf CAGRs are attributable net income CAGRs (FY2022->FY2025 and FY2020->FY2025): the statutory FCF series swings from -5.7bn to +4.8bn with lease originations and is meaningless as an owner-cash-flow history. Revenue: FY2020 8,521 -> FY2022 12,073 -> FY2025 14,940. EPS (diluted, RMB): 0.96 -> 0.93 -> 1.08. Attributable equity: 10,771 -> 13,980 -> 19,281. Attributable NI: 1,648 -> 1,888 -> 2,157.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2026 -5%: H1 was -6.3% with both segments down; H2 FY2025 comp (7,359) is softer than H1's and the FY2025 healthcare-tech acquisitions annualise. FY2027 +2% as the finance book stops shrinking (interest-earning assets 71.1bn at June 2026, back above the FY2025 close) and hospital volumes grow with the aging population; 3-3.5% thereafter, settling at 3%.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Margin here is (PBT + D&A)/revenue, after funding costs and impairments. FY2025 25.5%; H1 FY2026 annualised 30.3% because costs fell faster than revenue. FY2026E 27.3% = PBT ~3,050 (H1 1,746 + a typical ~1,300 H2; H2 PBT was 1,278 in FY2025 and 1,288 in FY2024) plus D&A ~830 on revenue ~14,190. Drifts to 26% as the mix shifts toward lower-margin healthcare and the funding-cost tailwind that lifted NIM to 4.4% fades.
base.capex_pct_rationale: capex minus D&A = 4.1-4.2% of revenue = ~RMB590-740m/yr of retained equity: 23% attributable-equity-to-assets on ~3% asset growth (~600m) plus hospital capex modestly above D&A. Equivalent to a ~27% retention ratio (g/ROE = 3%/11.5%). The remaining retained earnings beyond this (the company pays only 30%) go to deleveraging, which accrues to equity holders and is not a further deduction.
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: (income tax 701.6 + NCI 108.6 + perpetual coupons 52.2) / PBT 3,019.1 = 28.5% FY2025; H1 FY2026 27.7%. Statutory PRC rate 25% with hospital subsidiaries partly tax-exempt; minorities and perpetuals included so post-tax EBIT is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders.

bull.rationale: Healthcare-technology (+75% FY2025) and specialty medical ('1+N' ophthalmology, TCM, rehab) scale and lift margins; DRG/DIP pressure on integrated hospitals plateaus after the FY2025-26 reset; finance NIM holds near 4.3% with NPL ~1% and 339% coverage; equity capital needed only for 2.5% asset growth (retention 3.5% of revenue); SOE 'Valuation Enhancement Plan' and strategic shareholders narrow the governance discount (CoE 10.5%).

bear.rationale: DRG/DIP reform keeps cutting reimbursement per treatment so the integrated-hospital segment turns loss-making at the PBT line; D&A keeps rising on the ~RMB5bn of hospital infrastructure commissioned since 2024; finance NIM normalises back toward the FY2023 3.2% as funding-cost declines end while asset yields keep repricing, and credit costs rise as hospital borrowers come under the same reimbursement stress (NPL toward 2%). ROE compresses to ~7-8%. SASAC-directed hospital consolidation keeps capex above D&A by 5.5% of revenue, and higher NPL requires more equity per asset. CoE 13.5% for credit-cycle, refinancing and governance risk.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue dips 5% in FY2026 (H1 -6.3%) then grows 2-3.5% as the lease book stabilises around RMB71bn and hospital volumes recover; attributable profit holds ~RMB2.2bn in FY2026 (H1 +2.8%) on lower funding costs and cost control, then compounds at ~3% with the (PBT+D&A) margin drifting from 27.3% to 26% as the mix shifts to healthcare. FCFE is attributable profit less ~RMB600-740m/yr of equity retained for 3% asset growth and hospital capex above D&A; 30% payout continues and the balance of retention keeps deleveraging. Discounted at an 11.5% CNY cost of equity, terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Healthcare-technology and specialty-medical growth plus a plateau in DRG/DIP pressure lift the margin toward 28%; revenue regrows 4-5% from FY2027; finance NIM holds ~4.3% with benign credit; only 3.5% of revenue needs retaining; governance discount narrows (CoE 10.5%, terminal growth 3%).
scenario_narratives.bear: Reimbursement reform deepens, the hospital segment loses money at PBT, D&A keeps rising on commissioned capex, NIM normalises to ~3.2% and credit costs rise; ROE falls to ~7-8%; SOE-directed capex keeps retention at 5.5% of revenue; revenue -8% then flat for three years. CoE 13.5%, terminal growth 1.5%. This case lands near the current quote, i.e. the market is pricing roughly this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Skewed to bear (35/45/20) rather than the house 25/50/25 or 15/50/35. The 0.38x book / 3.5x earnings quote reflects durable discounts (central-SOE capital allocation that can follow SASAC rather than shareholders, a wholesale-funded lender with no deposit franchise, structural DRG/DIP reimbursement headwinds that already cut hospital segment profit 39% in FY2025 and 24% in H1 FY2026, and thin HK liquidity). Those are reasons the gap to intrinsic value may not close, and the bear case embeds a credit-cycle outcome that the lender's 1% NPL has not yet tested. Bull capped at 20% because the two segments' growth engines (healthcare tech, specialty medical) are small relative to the leasing book that drives 84% of profit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the equity flow a lender actually produces (attributable profit less the equity it must retain to carry asset growth), at the cost of equity, with borrowings treated as operating funding of the RMB71bn lease book rather than net debt. The hospital business is consolidated into the same flow because it is funded from the same balance sheet and, at 17% of PBT, is a margin driver rather than a separable franchise. The quote at 0.38x book and ~8% dividend yield means the market already assumes something close to the bear case; the valuation question is how much of the SOE/policy discount is permanent, which the bear-heavy weighting and the 11.5-13.5% costs of equity are meant to carry.
key_risks_to_valuation: DRG/DIP reimbursement reform turning the integrated-hospital segment structurally loss-making (segment PBT already -39% FY2025, -24% H1 FY2026 on growing revenue); the bear margin path assumes this

Finance NIM normalising from 4.4% back toward the FY2023 3.2% level once the funding-cost tailwind ends, with credit costs rising if hospital borrowers (including related-party and SOE hospitals) come under reimbursement stress; NPL ~1% and 339% coverage have not been through a credit cycle

Refinancing: RMB49.5bn of bank lines, bonds (CULC approved for up to RMB8bn), perpetuals and sale-and-leaseback funding; any loss of central-SOE funding access would hit both the spread and the going-concern premise of the lender

SOE capital allocation: SASAC-mandated hospital consolidation or sub-CoE hospital capex could absorb retained earnings beyond the modelled 4-5.5% of revenue; the 30% payout is the floor the model relies on, not the full FCFE
Dilution: the FY2025 convertible conversion and placements added 6.5% to the share count; a further discounted placement to 'optimise the financial structure' is not modelled
CNY/HKD: the HKD per-share values move one-for-one with the 1.1756 bridge; CNY depreciation lowers the HKD value and the HKD-declared dividend coverage

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for 2666.HK at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX intraday); 52-week range 4.32-6.67 HKD. FX bridge from USDHKD=X and USDCNY=X at the same timestamp.
